fabrics.name: Piña
fabrics.description: A fine, sheer cloth handwoven from pineapple-leaf fibers. It is light, slightly stiff, and has a soft natural sheen.
identifyingFeatures: See-through when held up to light

steps: Hand wash only, in cool water (below 30 °C).
Add a few drops of mild, pH-neutral soap.
Swish gently for 2–3 minutes. Do not rub, twist or wring.
Rinse twice in clean, cool water.
Roll the garment in a clean towel and press to remove water.
Hang on a padded hanger or lay flat, in the shade.
Keep out of direct sun. Sunlight yellows natural fibers.
Iron while the fabric is still slightly damp.
Iron on the reverse side, with a thin cotton press cloth on top.
Press and lift. Do not slide the iron over embroidery.

setting.text: Low, up to 110 °C, with a press cloth

steps: Blot (do not rub) with a clean, dry cloth.
For oil, sprinkle cornstarch or baby powder on it. Wait 15 minutes, then brush it off.
Dab with cool water and one drop of mild soap.
Rinse with cool water and air dry.
Mix 1 tablespoon of white vinegar in 1 litre of cool water.
Soak the area for 15 minutes.
Rinse well in clean, cool water.
Do not use hot water. Heat sets the stain.
Scrape off any extra with a blunt edge.
Dab with mild dish soap on a cotton swab, from the outside in.
Rinse with cool water.
Test on a hidden seam first.
Dab with rubbing alcohol on a cotton swab. Blot with a clean cloth.
Repeat until no more ink lifts, then rinse.
Store only when clean and fully dry.
Wrap in acid-free tissue or a clean cotton cloth.
Hang on a padded hanger or roll it. Avoid sharp folds.
Keep away from damp. Add silica gel packs.

fabrics.name: Cocoon
fabrics.description: A light fabric with a built-in crinkled texture, so it looks fine even when wrinkled. Popular for everyday barong.

steps: Turn the garment inside out.
Hand wash, or machine wash on gentle inside a mesh bag.

Iron on the reverse side only.

Keep the iron moving. High heat can melt synthetic fibers.

fabrics.name: Wool suiting
fabrics.description: A smooth, firm woven wool used for suits and slacks. It drapes well and resists wrinkles.

steps: Dry cleaning is safest for tailored suits.
To hand wash, use cold water and a wool soap. Do not soak long.
Never wring or rub; wool shrinks and felts.
Lay flat on a towel, away from heat and sun.
Reshape while damp.
Brush lightly with a clothes brush once dry.
Use steam and a damp press cloth.
Press and lift. Do not slide.
Let it cool on the hanger before wearing.
